literal: Ruin plotting than a minister by the side, enemy a seventy crore is better.
translation: It is better to face seventy crore open enemies than to have a minister by one's side who secretly plots ruin.
modern: தனக்குக் கேடு விளைவிக்க நினைக்கும் அமைச்சர் தன் பக்கத்தில் இருப்பதை விட, எழுபது கோடி எதிரிகளைப் பெற்றிருப்பது மேலானது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the extreme danger of a treacherous advisor. The phrase 'பழுது எண்ணும்' describes a minister who secretly plots harm or ruin against their own leader. The word 'தெவ்' means enemy, and the poet uses the massive number 'ஓர் எழுபது கோடி' (seventy crores) to represent an overwhelming external threat. The verb 'உறும்' indicates that facing this unimaginable number of open enemies is preferable. The core message is that an internal threat disguised as a trusted minister is far more destructive than any external force.
